kevin: FYI rolled kernel-selector tweak (affinity fallback) to canary this morning. Seeing ~12% p95 regression on small-chat prefill-heavy traffic. p50 26ms -> 28ms, p95 88ms -> 103ms. Anyone else?

sylvia: yep, spotted it on the perf dashboard :eyes:. traces show more prefill batches hitting generic kernel during the handshake. KV warmup miss rate also ticked up.

kevin: quick profile snippet I grabbed from the canary host:
```text
[prof] 00:00:00.012 kernel_affine  35ms (30%)
[prof] 00:00:00.047 kernel_generic 48ms (41%)  <-- up from 35ms
[prof] 00:00:00.095 kv_warmup      12ms (10%)  <-- more misses
[prof] 00:00:00.107 queue_wait     8ms  ( 7%)
```

ron: did the canary touch batcher token_budget or queue bias? I thought the change was just kernel selection fallback. Could be a small timing shift causing batch formation to change.

marta: I ran a quick local canary: reduced prefill token_target 64 -> 48 and turned on strict phase separation. p95 improved to ~94ms (was 103ms) but overall throughput dropped ~3%. tradeoff.

kevin: can you paste the config you used? also want kv hit/miss numbers if you have them.

marta: config I used:
```yaml
batcher:
  phase_separation: true
  token_target:
    prefill: 48
    decode: 12
queue_policy:
  bias: phase_priority
kernel_selector:
  fallback_threshold: 0.7
  prefer_affine: true
```
kv stats for that run: hit_rate prefill 86% -> 92% with separation, but avg tokens/batch reduced (~+/- smaller batches).

perf-bot: automated summary (1m sample): prefill->generic fallback +22%, kv_warmup miss-rate +11%, kernel_generic cpu time +36%, tail latency delta +15% (link: http://perf/reports/3280012345).

sylvia: hypothesis: the affinity change adds a small scheduling cost in the hot path which pushes a subset of prefill windows over our kernel threshold, causing fallback -> higher generic runtime + more KV misses. Fix options:
1) raise prefill token_target (bigger batches)
2) lower fallback_threshold temporarily so we force affine more often
3) insert micro-prefill (4 tokens) to prime KV for tiny chats
4) tweak queue bias to prefer prefill coalescing

kevin: i'm going to try (2) lowering fallback_threshold 0.7 -> 0.6 first (cheap), and (3) micro-prefill trial on canary (4 tokens). will enable TRACE_KERNEL=1 for richer traces.

marta: micro-prefill helped in my local runs but watch cost/throughput. also enabling TRACE_KERNEL will add noise; sample for 5-10 minutes only.

ron: SGTM. if canary improves p95 without killing throughput we can iterate. if not, revert selector change. :thumbsup:

kevin: launching canary tweak now (fallback_threshold=0.6 + micro-prefill=4). I'll post results in ~10min.

sylvia: thanks — adding a perf dashboard card and KV hit/miss alert for the canary.

kevin: result (10m): fallback rate down 9%, p95 back to ~90ms, throughput -0.7%. KV miss-rate down 6%. Looks promising. leaving canary running and collecting traces. :+1:

ron: nice. next steps: run 1h experiment, validate with bursty small-chat traces, then document scheduler knob defaults.

marta: will draft a short runbook for ops (how to tune token_target, fallback_threshold, micro-prefill tradeoffs).
